what: Phase 3 of the estate go-live: the mesh is live. The foundation's nodes, each its own operating-system process, find each other through thin relays, route asks by competence, route around a node that dies, keep shared state consistent by CRDT, and share immunity, and the mesh keeps going when a relay dies. Sealed before relay.mjs, the node's new verbs, the sync kernel or any measuring code for Phase 3 exists. One organ per pass; a claim not yet measured says so.
scope: One machine: every node and every relay is its own operating-system process, and they exchange only bytes over local TCP. Browsers join in pass 5 over real WebRTC between two tabs. A second device is a door the owner opens from the page; it is not claimed here.

A relay is transport, not trust: it reads only the recipient named on a frame and never a body. Every body is a LIGHT packet the sending node signed, checked by the receiving node's own door, so a relay that lies, drops, reorders or replays is caught there or costs only delivery.

The hostile nodes in pass 4 send the kinds of packet the door is built to refuse (unpinned, forged, changed, replayed, junk) and variants of them. No model writes them. A real outside adversary against the live mesh is the owner's to invite; it is not claimed here.

The CRDT is last-writer-wins by Lamport time with the node id as tie-break (fallsync's rule, gated in its own repository first): it converges; it does not merge two people's edits to one key into one.

passes.organ: the mesh joins and routes (core/node.mjs: expire, roster)
shared state by CRDT (fallsync's kernel, vendored; core/node.mjs: sync)
browsers on the mesh over WebRTC

claims.claim: A relay carries bytes and reads nothing else: it forwards each frame by the recipient it names, and no body is ever decoded at a relay.
claims.measure: every frame through the relays in the mesh run; the relay's own code checked for any import of the codec, the door or the vault
claims.holds_if: every frame delivered to the node it named, the relays decode 0 bodies, and relay.mjs imports none of the codec, the door or the vault

claims.claim: Any relay can die and the mesh goes on: with one of two relays killed mid-run, every later ask still completes through the other, and no node loses any state.
claims.measure: eight nodes on two relays; relay A killed after the first round of asks
claims.holds_if: every ask after the kill answered; every node's ledger, memory and couplings the same as a run where nothing was killed, up to the kill, and moving on after

claims.claim: A node that is away gets what was sent to it when it comes back, once: a relay holds frames for an absent node, and a copy delivered twice is refused at the node's door.
claims.measure: a node disconnected while asks are sent to it, then reconnected; the relay told to deliver its queue twice
claims.holds_if: every frame sent while it was away is delivered on return, and every second copy is refused at the counter

claims.claim: A node joins the mesh by the founder's roster: it pins every member the roster names and refuses a card the roster does not.
claims.measure: eight nodes and a founder-signed roster of them; a ninth card not on the roster offered to every node; a roster signed by another key
claims.holds_if: every node pins exactly the seven others, refuses the ninth, and refuses the roster not signed by the founder

claims.claim: Asks go to a node that holds the skill, and to the one whose answers check.
claims.measure: 100 asks across the mesh for skills held by some nodes, one holder of triage dishonest
claims.holds_if: every ask goes to a holder of its skill, and after the first 20, at least 90% of triage asks go to an honest holder

claims.claim: A node that dies is routed around: its unanswered asks expire, its coupling falls, and its skill is asked of another holder.
claims.measure: a triage holder killed mid-run; the next 40 triage asks
claims.holds_if: at most 2 asks go to the dead node before every later one goes to a live holder, and every later ask is answered

claims.claim: Couplings follow evidence at the size of the mesh, as they did for two nodes: the honest holder's link outgrows the dishonest one's at every asker.
claims.measure: each of the four askers' links to the honest and the dishonest triage holder after the run
claims.holds_if: at every asker the honest link is above the dishonest link, and the dishonest one is below the floor

claims.claim: Shared state converges: every node ends with the same shared map, whatever order the updates arrive in.
claims.measure: eight nodes each writing to one shared map, the updates carried as signed LIGHT packets through the relays in three different shuffled orders, with a relay killed in one of them
claims.holds_if: in every order, every node's map has the same digest at the end, and the three orders give the same digest

claims.claim: Only a pinned member can change the shared state: a sync from a key not on the roster, or one changed in transit, changes nothing.
claims.measure: sync packets from a stranger and changed copies of real ones, sent to every node
claims.holds_if: 0 of them change any node's map, each refused at the door

claims.claim: Herd immunity: an attack one node refuses is, after one round of sharing, recognised on sight by every node in the mesh.
claims.measure: a hostile packet refused at one node; its antibodies shared through the relays; the same bytes then sent to all eight
claims.holds_if: every node adopts after re-running it on its own door, and all eight then refuse it as recognised, without decoding

claims.claim: A crowd of hostile nodes gets nothing through: none of what sixteen unpinned or forging nodes send is admitted anywhere, and variants of a learned attack are recognised as its family.
claims.measure: sixteen hostile processes each sending unpinned, forged, changed, replayed and junk packets, and variants of them, to every node
claims.holds_if: 0 admitted at any node, 0 decoded, and at least half of the variants named as a variant of a family already learned
claims.predicted: unsure — the variant share depends on how close the variants fall to the shapes learned first

claims.claim: Immunity never turns on the mesh itself: after all the learning, every node still admits every packet its pinned peers sign.
claims.measure: after H1 and H2, 100 ordinary asks and answers across the mesh
claims.holds_if: every one admitted and answered, none refused as recognised

claims.claim: A browser is a node on the mesh: two tabs connect over a real WebRTC data channel and exchange signed LIGHT packets that each one's door checks.
claims.measure: two browser tabs on one device, connected by WebRTC (offer and answer carried same-device), each running a foundation node
claims.holds_if: the data channel opens, every signed packet is admitted, a changed one and a replayed one are refused at their stages
